asOf: Market data as of 26 Oct 2026 (Kalyan Jewellers: close of 23 Oct 2026)
basis: Company figures FY25 audited and FY26 provisional, valuation at the round's ₹125 Cr pre-money; peers FY26 (year to Mar 2026) consolidated annual results and market capitalisation on 23–26 Oct 2026.

companies.name: Jandani Jewellers Limited
companies.note: Indore jewellery manufacturer and retailer with an in-house manufacturing technology unit (CGT); 1 company store and 3 franchises; pre-money valuation of the round.

companies.name: Senco Gold Limited
companies.note: Kolkata-based national jewellery retailer (201 showrooms); also Jandani's store-in-store partner, so both a peer and a customer.

companies.name: Kalyan Jewellers India Limited
companies.note: Largest listed jewellery retailer by revenue (507 showrooms in India, Middle East, UK, US); grows through franchise-owned showrooms, the route Jandani is taking.

companies.name: Thangamayil Jewellery Limited
companies.note: Madurai-based regional chain (66+ stores across Tamil Nadu); a regional retailer that scaled from a single home market.

companies.name: Sky Gold and Diamonds Limited
companies.note: Navi Mumbai B2B gold jewellery manufacturer supplying organised retailers and export; peer to Jandani's manufacturing and supply business.

companies.name: RBZ Jewellers Limited
companies.note: Ahmedabad antique-jewellery maker with one retail showroom and B2B supply to ~190 retailers; the closest listed peer in size and model.

dims.name: Product / technology
dims.why: Jandani runs an in-house manufacturing technology unit (CGT) that contributed about ₹15 Cr of FY26 revenue, and it supplies Senco Gold. The process is disclosed only in general terms. Sky Gold has comparable depth in lightweight manufacturing at far larger volume. The retail chains mostly source from outside manufacturers.

dims.name: Customers and concentration
dims.why: Jandani's revenue comes from one company store, three franchises and a store-in-store arrangement with Senco Gold, whose volumes are not yet fixed. The listed retailers sell to millions of retail customers across 66 to 507 stores.

dims.name: Entry barriers
dims.why: In jewellery retail the protection comes from brand trust and access to gold funding. Kalyan and Senco have both at national scale. Jandani's main protection is its manufacturing process, which investors cannot yet verify.

dims.name: Distribution / reach
dims.why: Jandani has 4 stores in four cities and plans to open Pune and Bhopal franchises in FY27. Kalyan has 507 showrooms in four countries, Senco 201, and Thangamayil 66+ in one state. RBZ has 1 showroom plus B2B supply to about 190 retailers.

dims.name: Scale of operations
dims.why: Jandani's FY26 revenue of ₹84.9 Cr is 13% of RBZ's (₹636 Cr) and 0.2% of Kalyan's (₹35,743 Cr).

dims.name: Management and governance
dims.why: Jandani was incorporated as a public limited company in 2024, and its FY26 accounts are still provisional, with completion conditional on audit. The listed peers publish audited results every quarter. Sky Gold's operating cash flow was negative in both FY25 and FY26.

dims.name: Growth runway
dims.why: Jandani grew revenue 92% in FY26 and projects ₹164 Cr for FY27 (93% growth) through franchises and Senco supply. Peers grew 20–77% in FY26, partly because gold prices rose.

dims.name: Gold working capital access
dims.why: The company names gold working capital, not equipment, as the limit on the technology unit; ₹7.25 Cr of the ₹12.5 Cr round goes there. Listed peers fund inventory through bank lines and gold metal loans, with debt to equity between 0.47x and 1.07x.

dims.name: Brand strength
dims.why: Jandani is a single-city brand that is starting to enter other cities through franchises. Kalyan and Senco are national consumer brands, and Thangamayil is a strong regional one. Sky Gold and RBZ mostly sell under other retailers' brands.

matrix.why: Jandani combines manufacturing and retail, as RBZ does, while the large peers are mainly retailers or mainly manufacturers.

matrix.why: Jandani sells in four cities in western and central India. Its peers are present across a state, a region or the whole country.

matrix.why: Jandani has 4 stores against 66–507 at the retail peers. RBZ has a similar retail footprint, with one showroom.

matrix.why: Kalyan also expands through franchise-owned showrooms. Jandani's franchisees buy their stock upfront, so it extends no gold credit to them.
Jandani is the smallest company in the set, about one-seventh the size of RBZ.
Jandani reported the fastest growth and the highest PAT margin in the set, on provisional figures from a small base.

cells: Store-in-store supplier to Senco (first order: bangles)
matrix.why: Jandani, like RBZ, supplies a listed retailer, but its Senco volumes are not yet committed.

cells: Round funds ₹7.25 Cr working capital; debt not disclosed
Debt/equity 0.71x; negative operating cash flow FY26
matrix.why: The listed peers have bank and gold-loan lines in place. Jandani is raising equity to fund gold.
The round closes only after Jandani's FY26 audit is complete. The listed peers report every quarter.
The round prices Jandani at 12.5x FY26 PAT. The peer range is 8.7x (Senco) to 57.7x (Sky Gold), with a median of 39.2x.

barriers.name: Brand trust
barriers.note: Buyers of gold jewellery pay a premium for brands they trust. Jandani's brand is established in Indore but is still new in the franchise cities.

barriers.name: Gold working capital
barriers.note: Growth requires funding gold inventory. Jandani says gold funding is its constraint, and 58% of the round is going to it.

barriers.name: Manufacturing process know-how
barriers.note: The technology unit's process is proprietary and gave about ₹15 Cr of FY26 revenue. It has not been shown to investors in detail, so how much it protects the business cannot be judged from outside.

barriers.name: Relationships with listed retailers
barriers.note: The Senco store-in-store arrangement is an approved-vendor relationship that is hard to obtain. So far only a first bangles order has been placed, and annual volumes are not fixed.

barriers.name: Franchise network
barriers.note: Three franchises are open and two more are planned for FY27. Because franchisees pay for stock upfront, Jandani's credit risk is low, but the network is not yet large enough to deter competitors.

barriers.name: Hallmarking and compliance
barriers.note: BIS hallmarking and HUID rules apply to every jeweller in the set. They raise the cost of operating for all of them rather than favouring any one company.

ahead: Fastest growth in the set: revenue up 91.6% in FY26 (₹44.3 Cr to ₹84.9 Cr) against 20–77% at listed peers.
Highest PAT margin: 11.8% in FY26 against 3.8–8.6% at peers (Kalyan 3.8%, Senco 6.8%, RBZ 8.6%).
Owns its manufacturing, including a technology unit (about ₹15 Cr of FY26 revenue), and supplies Senco Gold under a store-in-store arrangement.
behind: Smallest in the set: FY26 revenue of ₹84.9 Cr is about 13% of RBZ's ₹636 Cr and 0.2% of Kalyan's ₹35,743 Cr.
4 stores in four cities, against 66 to 507 showrooms at the listed retailers.
FY26 figures are provisional and the round is conditional on audit; the peers report audited results every quarter.
Gold working capital limits growth; listed peers already carry bank and gold-loan lines (debt to equity 0.47–1.07x).

The FY26 margins of all peers include gains from higher gold prices; Senco puts its sustainable EBITDA margin at 7.5–7.7% against 11.5% reported. The subject's 11.8% PAT margin has not been split the same way.
watch: Audited FY26 accounts confirming ₹84.9 Cr revenue and ₹10.0 Cr PAT.
Annual volumes under the Senco store-in-store arrangement beyond the first bangles order.
Opening of the Pune (Q3 FY27) and Bhopal (Q4 FY27) franchises on schedule.
FY27 progress against the ₹164 Cr revenue / ₹15.3 Cr PAT projection, and the effect of gold price moves on margins.
valuation: P/E at the round is 12.5x FY26 PAT (pre-money), against a peer median of 39.2x; RBZ trades at 12.6x and Senco at 8.7x.
